report.md:
## This week
12 posts this week, same as prior week, both all talking-head. Median views fell from 2472 to 1827.5. The standout was "First I went to TikTok and looked up U.G.C." at 12,100 views. The clearest dud with a full day to breathe is "Not every decision has to be the right one" at 821 views (the 15-view post is only hours old, too new to call).

## Format or script?
Format explains almost none of the variance in views (0.028), but that's mostly because she's barely varied it: 93 of her 124 tagged videos are talking-head, and both this week and last week were 12/12 talking-head. There are no repeated-script pairs in the data to compare formats head to head on the same content. What separates videos more is structure (0.112) and topic bucket (0.11), and cta explains more than any other axis (0.221). At this level of evidence, topic and structure choices look like they're doing more work than format, but that read is soft because format hasn't really been tested. Skit (n=2) and photo-carousel (n=2), despite huge multiples, are too few videos to judge.

## What is working
The-come-up bucket is a genuine strength: 22 videos, median 7383 views, 1.94x the catalog median, and 4 of her top 10. Longer videos also stand out: the 8 videos at 60s+ post a median of 23,550 views, 6.19x catalog. Link-in-bio CTA videos (n=6) show a median of 69,550 views, 18.27x catalog, and 4 top-10 spots, though with only 6 videos this should be watched, not fully trusted yet.

## Try next week
Post more the-come-up content and specifically try it as broll-voiceover or skit, since within that bucket talking-head sits at a 2833 median while broll-voiceover hits 20,700 and skit hits 27,000, though those are only 3 and 2 videos so treat it as a lead, not proof. Add a link-in-bio CTA to more videos to see if the 69,550 median holds up with more volume. Deliberately shoot a few more 60s+ videos, since that duration only has 8 videos behind its 6.19x catalog median, to find out if length itself is the driver.

best.md: This video is a clear outperformer, pulling 12,100 views against a catalog median of 3,806 and beating out its format, bucket, and hook medians too. The hook "First I went to TikTok and looked up U.G.C." works because it drops straight into step one of a process, which grabs attention through direct value rather than a cold tease, but it skips planting an actual curiosity seed in seconds 3-6, it just keeps stacking steps. What saves it is that the value never stops paying out: research, template, product, upload, apply to Kora, UGC Tank, Reddit, book 10 deals, that's a real specific path with numbers in it, and specificity is what's driving the repeat watches. There is no CTA at all, which the tags confirm and the transcript backs up, so you're leaving views on the table by not asking for a follow or comment at the very last second when the value has already landed. Fix for next time: keep the exact structure and hook style, just tack one line onto the end asking viewers to comment "deals" or follow for the template.

worst.md: This is an underperformer at 1185 views against a catalog median of 3806, and it also lags its own format, bucket, and hook benchmarks. The hook "One of the most freeing things was realizing that I can literally just leave" states a conclusion instead of opening a gap, so there's no real curiosity seed planted in seconds 3-6, it just restates the same idea (job, a man, a situation) without new information. At only 12 seconds there isn't room for value to keep paying off, the video ends right where the insight should start getting concrete or personal. With no CTA at all, it also forfeits the easiest lever available at the very end. This is a moment-clip that needed either a sharper contradiction up front or a specific story beat to earn the back half.
